title: Can the grid trust a fast AI answer?
prompt:
Create a large 16:9 landscape infographic for a general professional audience (managers, engineers new to the topic, students), light near-white background, warm and clear like a well-designed museum explainer or a quality newspaper graphic. Plain everyday language is the main text; technical names appear only as small grey secondary labels.

TITLE (large): "Can the grid trust a fast AI answer?"
SUBTITLE: "An AI model predicted six power-flow solutions in milliseconds. TOKN checked each against physics before an operator could act."

BAND 1 — heading "Why this matters": one wide card with a simple flat illustration of a transmission tower with a lightning-fast stopwatch, and this text: "AI models solve grid equations far faster than classical solvers, but a wrong answer could overload a line. Speed only helps once it is verified."

BAND 2 — heading "Who did the work": a left-to-right flow of eight round role badges joined by arrows. Each badge shows a line icon, the bold role name, the short description in quotes, and the model name tiny and grey below:
1 Scout — "lists the tools available" (claude-haiku-5.5) [icon: binoculars]
2 Planner — "writes what 'done' looks like" (claude-opus-5.5) [icon: document]
3 Analyst — "runs the official checks" (Kimi-K3.1-Pro) [icon: bar chart]
4 Skeptic — "re-checks and finds 9 weak spots" (FW-GLM-5.3) [icon: shield]
5 Judge — "decides: revise or ship?" (Microsoft-Decision-1) [icon: balance scale]
6 Editor — "fixes every weak spot" (gpt-6.1-sol) [icon: pencil]
7 Coach — "writes a lesson for next time" (claude-opus-5.5) [icon: lightbulb]
8 Examiner — "scores it with plain code, no AI" (verify.py) [icon: checklist]
Caption under the flow: "Like a newsroom: a writer, a fact-checker, an editor — and an exam nobody can sweet-talk."

BAND 3 — heading "Four questions every AI answer must answer": four cards in a row, each with an icon, the question in large plain words, and a tiny grey tool label:
(balance scale icon) "Does power in equal power out?" — tiny grey label: verify_surrogate_solution
(gauge icon) "Are lines and voltages within limits?" — tiny grey label: verify_surrogate_solution
(stopwatch icon) "Does it speed up the classical solver?" — tiny grey label: evaluate_warm_start
(compass icon) "Is the situation unlike anything it was trained on?" — tiny grey label: assess_ood

BAND 4 — heading "What it found": 6 result cards in a row. Each shows the small ID at top, a large verdict word in its color with a matching status icon, and one plain sentence:
PRED-A — green (#16A34A) verdict "Advisory" — "Physics checks pass; it may inform the operator."
PRED-B — amber (#D97706) verdict "Hold for review" — "Physics passes, but the AI flagged its own answer as infeasible."
PRED-C — red (#DC2626) verdict "Reject" — "Power doesn't balance (-0.15 pu)."
PRED-D — green (#16A34A) verdict "Advisory" — "Values sit exactly on the limits, which is allowed."
PRED-E — red (#DC2626) verdict "Reject" — "Line and voltage limits broken, and it slows the solver."
PRED-F — blue (#2563EB) verdict "Warm start only" — "One generator over its limit, but it speeds the solver up 1.75×."
Small note at the right of the heading: "Physics decides; the AI's own confidence is never counted as evidence."

BOTTOM BAND — three short panels:
"Trust, but verify" — "An independent checker re-ran the checks and plain code graded the result: 6 of 6 correct."
"Honest wording" — "Every action on the grid stays human-approved."
"Getting better each run" — "The lesson saved for next time: Copy every number from a stored tool output; never retype it."

FOOTER (small, centered): "The takeaway: Fast is useful. Fast and verified is deployable."

TEXT DISCIPLINE: use ONLY the words given above in quotes plus the headings. Do NOT add any slogans, taglines, mottos, handwritten notes, brand lines, decorative words, extra footers or invented statistics. Every word spelled exactly as given and legible at 4K.

Visual rules: generous whitespace, strong hierarchy (title > band headings > plain sentences > tiny grey technical labels), verdict colors only on the result cards, soft blue/teal section tints, flat friendly line icons. No people, no faces, no photos.
